correctness.rationale: Correct over every field, with closure understood as geometric Zariski closure of the automorphism locus, not closure of the finite group of rational points. In the basis e=e1−e2, f=e2, z, only [e,f]=z survives. Preservation of the derived line gives a free central row and quotient block A=[[a,b],[c,d]]; the equations eliminate t=ad and leave ac=bc=bd=0. This is the intersection of the coordinate ideals (b,c), (a,b), (c,d); each component with the two central coordinates is A^4. Their pairwise dimensions are 3,3,2 and triple dimension 2. The principal open ad≠0 of the diagonal component is exactly the unit locus. Inclusion–exclusion gives 3L^4−2L^3 and exponentiating extension-field counts gives the asserted zeta function. In the two singular row planes each nonzero block admits q central rows of rank one and q²−q rows of rank two; the zero block and units give the remaining ranks. Each nonzero singular projection has one of the two row-type image lines, q complementary kernels and q choices of lift, so each lift occurs q times. A singular quotient block is nilpotent iff its trace is zero; the two trace-zero lines meet only at zero, and the central row remains free. An independent basis-product enumeration at q=2,3,5 checked rank counts (1,15,12,4), (1,56,96,36), (1,264,960,400), idempotent totals 10,20,52, nilpotent totals 12,45,225 and 2q proper retracts with q idempotents per retract. The field-independent proof, not these tests, establishes all quantifiers. The singular components meet the automorphism closure; only their points outside the diagonal component are outside the closure.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Even though J_q is stated over finite fields, its explicit polynomial equations contain no field-dependent step and give the scheme geometry over arbitrary fields in the same coordinates. The distinct paper on bilinear forms is not needed for this implication.

evidence: The two unrestricted singular row planes and diagonal graph s=ad are precisely the three components after conjugation. Setting the diagonal entries as required gives the intersections and unit closure. Trace zero selects one axis in each singular row plane; the idempotence conditions supply the two image lines and their arbitrary central lifts.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The unlisted nilpotent count, retract description, Grothendieck class and zeta function are direct trace, image and inclusion–exclusion consequences of the explicit polynomial and row-type split. They do not supply a genuinely distinct repair.

originality.rationale: A distinct Resultary record covers the same algebra, not a second rank-one algebra: using e=e1−e2, f=e2, z gives its sole product [e,f]=z in every characteristic. Its proof gives exactly the same equations and singular/diagonal split. Counts and component geometry either coincide or are immediate consequences of that split. This is demonstrable mathematical coverage, not a conclusion about chronological priority.
residual_risks: The exact chronological priority and relationship between the two records are not established; the finding is rejected for demonstrable content coverage. The geometric closure is not a statement about density of finite-field rational automorphisms.
